startup.name: Revion
startup.description: Revion is building an operating system for automotive retail. Its first product automates the administrative work that takes 30 to 40 percent of a service technician's day, so dealerships and auto retailers can service more vehicles and earn more high margin revenue. Buyers are auto retail service departments. Team of 10 in New York City, Winter 2026 batch.

yc_acceptance.basis: Already in the batch, so this is reported for completeness only. Start from the roughly 1 percent prior for a random applicant in references/yc_acceptance.md (band 0.6 to 2 percent), then adjust: a clear paid pain and a ten person team lift it about 2x, an AI vertical that fits current YC interest adds a little, and the crowded dealer AI space takes some back; no traction is stated.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because dealer service AI had several funded players by late 2025, the input states no customers or revenue, and a technician assistant looks like a feature that dealer management vendors could ship. The acceptance estimate is a prior for a random applicant and does not rank this company, and since it is already in the batch it matters only as context for the ladder.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B: seed 47% / 53% / 59%, cond 53% (n=878). Timing: months_to_seed p25 4, p50 8, p75 20 (n=468).
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor of 0.53 is the ever reached figure. The window is only 10 months, so about 55 percent of eventual seed raisers have raised by then (median 8 months), giving about 0.29. I do not lift for the hot AI vertical or the team of 10, per the winners test rule, and this number does not rank Revion against other companies.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round of $1M to $3M from angels and micro funds, the YC deal alone (about $500K) is excluded by the seed definition. A seed right after Demo Day is the common time, and a 10 person team can use a larger round than a founder pair.
Institutional seed of $3M to $6M, near the 2022 and later median of $3.5M in round_benchmarks.csv, which includes the YC deal and reads low, so this band carries the most weight.
Larger institutional seed where press covered 2026 raises had a median of $6.0M (quartiles $4.3M and $10M, n=77, press leans to big rounds); needs live revenue or a standout team story.
Upside seed above $12M, seen in 2025 AI categories when several funds bid for a team with early enterprise traction.

ladder.why_it_fails: Dealer service AI is a crowded 2025 category with Toma (W24) already past a Series A and ShortLoop (W23) at seed, so investors will ask why Revion wins technician workflow instead of the phone or sales side. A first product for technicians has to prove time saved inside real shops and integrate with dealer management systems such as CDK and Tekion. Clearline (S22) restarted as a dealership product after a failed pivot and shows how slowly this niche converts into priced rounds.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B: series_a cond 26% (n=468), ever 14% known-only, range 12% to 25%. Timing: months_to_series_a p25 21, median 28 (n=123).
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is the ever reached figure. A Series A within 10 months of the batch start is rare because the p25 for months to Series A is 21, so the probability is far below the anchor and reflects only a breakout.

bands.rationale: Thin or small Series A, common for vertical software with early but modest revenue. Only a breakout ramp inside the first year would produce a Series A, so the thin band stays modest.
Central band around the 2022 and later Series A median of $15M (p25 $11M, p75 $21M).
Strong growth round led by a top tier fund.
Upside where the category is hot and revenue compounds fast.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A inside 10 months would need seven figure recurring revenue from dealer groups, which the fastest dealer AI companies reach only after about a year of selling. Toma (W24) needed about a year to reach seven figure revenue before its Series A, and ShortLoop (W23) has stayed at seed, so the window is too short unless Revion lands dealer groups unusually fast.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B: series_b cond 21% (n=123), ever 3% known-only.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is the ever reached rate given Series A. A Series B inside a window of 10 months is rare because months_to_series_b has a median of 32 to 47 months from the batch start in time_to_milestones.csv, so only a breakout gets there.

bands.rationale: Thin Series B or bridge round of $10M to $20M, typical when growth is real but slower than the Series A story promised and investors want to see more revenue.
Central band; the 2022 and later Series B median is $40M.
Hot company band; the 2022 and later post money median is $600M.
Breakout upside above $70M at a valuation near $1B, reached only by the few companies that compound revenue quickly after a Series A.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B inside the window would need scaling to hundreds of dealerships, which almost no company of this kind does in under two years. Toma (W24) took years from batch to a Series B in the researched data, and ShortLoop (W23) shows the same slow path, so the window is too short for this step unless the company breaks out early.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B: series_c cond 19% (n=26), ever 1% known-only.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is conditional on Series B and ever reached, from a tiny sample. Inside the window almost nobody reaches Series C, so I keep a low nonzero figure for a breakout path with several fast rounds.

bands.rationale: Thin extension or flat round of $20M to $40M, used when a company needs more runway before it proves a Series C story.
Central band; the 2022 and later Series C median is $74M.
Strong growth round of $80M to $150M led by a growth fund, tied to a clear revenue ramp and category leadership.
Category leader upside above $150M at a multibillion valuation, seen only for the few companies that win a large market outright.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C inside the window is close to impossible for a ten person company in its first year, which would need several consecutive hypergrowth rounds. The researched Series C companies such as Postscript (W19) took roughly four to five years from batch, and nothing visible today points to the category defining ramp that would be required.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely Revion stalls as one of many dealership AI tools: Tekion, CDK and other dealer management vendors ship technician assistants, dealer groups consolidate on one vendor, and the team pivots or is acqui-hired. Clearline (S22) restarted for dealerships after a failed LLM product and has no round, and ShortLoop has stayed at seed.

analogs.outcome_summary: Reached seven figure revenue in under a year and raised a $17M Series A in 2025; shows the upside path for a dealership wedge.

analogs.relevance: Winter 2023 phone AI for dealership revenue
analogs.outcome_summary: Raised a seed and no later round found; stuck at seed in the same buyer segment.
Pivoted after a failed first product, restarted for dealerships, still no priced round.

analogs.relevance: Summer 2017 managed marketplace for car services
analogs.outcome_summary: Raised a seed and was acquired; shows auto service ventures end as small exits.

killers.risk: Dealer management vendors ship the same assistant
killers.evidence: Tekion and mykaarma already sell service AI agents and own the data and integrations that a technician tool needs.
killers.mitigation: Own one workflow such as inspection notes to repair orders with measured shop hours saved.

killers.evidence: Technicians are not software buyers, the dealer principal is; the product must integrate with legacy DMS systems and prove time saved.
killers.mitigation: Sell to service directors with a per shop ROI and install in days.

killers.risk: Window too short for a priced round
killers.evidence: Winter 2026 seeds cluster at Demo Day, so a 10 month window catches only the early half of eventual raises.
killers.mitigation: Aim for revenue proof by Demo Day.

competition_now.name: Tekion service AI
competition_now.what: Dealer management platform with AI service agents that draft repair orders and summarize technician notes

competition_now.name: Fullbay AI service order
competition_now.what: Turns technician notes into service order text, vendor claims 20 percent less paperwork
competition_now.traction: Shop software installed base, claim unverified

competition_now.name: Manual notes by technicians and advisors (status quo)
competition_now.what: Paperwork done by hand after each job

technical_complexity.rationale: Speech to repair order drafting is easy to prototype; the hard parts are integrating with dealer management systems, handling parts and labor codes and reaching accuracy a service manager will trust. A small team can ship a narrow version in three months.

takeover_risk.rationale: DMS vendors already ship service AI and have the integrations, so a technician assistant is a feature for them within a year.

evidence.claim: A Motor report found nearly 68 percent of early adopters in dealership service report measurable AI benefits and 81 percent of dealers plan bigger AI budgets in 2025
One Mercedes-Benz dealership cut total repair order time from 6.5 to 4.3 days with AI, a single account

roadmap.goal: Prove time saved inside real service departments
actions: Measure technician hours recovered per week
roadmap.proof: Documented hours saved and a paid pilot

roadmap.goal: Turn pilots into recurring contracts at a dealer group
actions: Land one dealer group with 10 or more stores
Integrate with the two largest DMS vendors

roadmap.goal: Multi group sales motion beyond the first product
actions: Add a second workflow from the operating system pitch
Hire a dealer industry enterprise seller
roadmap.proof: $1M annual recurring revenue across 5 dealer groups

pros.evidence: Technician administrative time of 30 to 40 percent is a claim in the input, and dealers report adoption benefits in industry surveys.

pros.point: Dealer AI is proven to reach Series A
pros.evidence: Toma (W24) raised a Series A after fast revenue growth in the same buyer segment.

brand.name: Revion
strengths: Rev suggests revenue and revving engines
weaknesses: Invented name close to many Rev prefixed software companies
brand.rationale: A short invented name that hints at revenue and engines, but it sounds like many software names. YC cases such as Toma (W24) show a plain short name did not stop a dealer AI company from raising, so the name is neutral.

narrative.headline: A real dealership pain with strong comps, but a 10 month window makes a priced seed less likely than not.
narrative.general_summary: Revion automates technician paperwork for dealership service departments. The need is measurable and Toma shows dealership AI can raise a Series A, but the space was already crowded in January 2026 and DMS vendors ship similar assistants. The window is only 10 months, so the probability uses the B2B timing curve, not a lift for team size. A Series A inside the window is very unlikely. The odds do not rank Revion against other companies. The forecast window runs from the as of date to 2026-11-17, and later rounds are only counted if they close inside it.

assumptions: Only the input file was used about the company; no site, directory page or news about it was read.
Seed means a round above about $1M from outside investors, not the standard YC deal of about $500K, that closes inside the window.
The company is already in YC, so the acceptance figure is reported for completeness only.
Web search covered the market only. Results dated after the as of date or naming the company were to be ignored; none named it.
Funding coverage in the repo data is incomplete (see base_rates.py ranges), so the anchors are lower to upper ranges and not exact.
